tech_ai_semis.rationale: Facts: the midterm sweep put AI data-center limits on the agenda (Sanders 'national moratorium', 40 of 41 local measures lost, Texas Gov-elect Hinojosa's approval ban from Jan 19, Ohio's Acton) and SOX fell ~12% on Nov 5 (NVDA -9.3%, AMD -17%, MU -17%), spreading to Korea (KOSPI circuit breaker), Taiwan (stabilisation fund) and Japan (Nikkei bear market). The funding side is strained: Microsoft is winding down the Oracle rental and trimming neoclouds, Oracle raised $20B at 7-8.65% coupons and 11% below market, CoreWeave/Nebius roughly halved in a month, and crowded software winners de-rated (FTNT -31%, NOW -27%, DDOG -14%). Offsetting, demand data is intact: AMD data center +97%, Korea chip exports +259%, TSMC Q4 guide ~+14% q/q, Nvidia's own Q3 guide $108B, hyperscalers' own 2027 capex guided up, and chips rebounded 5-8% on Nov 6. Interpretation: a policy, financing and valuation unwind rather than a demand collapse; a federal moratorium is a long shot (needs reintroduction in 2027, no 60 Senate votes, veto) and state statute risk lands after the 1-3 month window, so -1 not -2. TSMC October sales (~Nov 10), CoreWeave/Nebius (Nov 10-12) and Nvidia (Nov 17) can move this either way.

us_large_broad.rationale: Facts: the S&P 500 fell ~4.4% on Nov 5 (worst day since April 2025) and ~2.7% on the week, the Nasdaq entered correction and the Magnificent Seven lost >$1T in a day; HY OAS widened 16bp to 348bp the same day while IG stayed at 93bp. Strong October payrolls (+165k) lifted December hike odds to ~75%, though the 10y rallied to ~4.84% and the Cleveland core CPI nowcast is a soft 0.21%. Breadth is healthy: equal-weight RSP, XLP, XLV and quality-dividend ETFs set records on Nov 4 and hyperscalers fell only 2-4%. Interpretation: the drag is concentrated in the ~third of cap-weighted indices tied to AI capex plus hike risk, so a mild headwind for cap-weighted trackers with low confidence; equal-weight is the better expression within the bucket. CPI/10y auction (Nov 10) and Nvidia (Nov 17) are the swing events; Dec 11 CR expiry is a secondary risk.

regime_notes: One AI-buildout factor drove the week: the midterm data-center backlash met existing AI-ROI and financing doubts (Microsoft's Oracle/neocloud pullback, Oracle's $20B raise, neocloud credit near distress), producing SOX -12% on Nov 5 and contagion across Korea, Taiwan, Japan, copper, merchant power, HY credit and small caps. Treat the resulting -1 scores across those buckets as one correlated bet, not independent views. Hard demand data (TSMC guide, Korea chip exports, AMD, Nvidia's guide, hyperscaler own capex) contradicts a demand collapse, so mean reversion is the base case unless the Nov 10-17 prints disappoint. Stress is on the funding side: watch CoreWeave, Nebius, Oracle spreads and Nvidia's $105B contingent guarantee on OpenAI leases. State and federal policy risk is mostly back-loaded (Congress Jan 3, Hinojosa Jan 19, ERCOT audit mid-December). Rates matter too: ~75% December hike odds against a 10y rally and soft core nowcast; Nov 10 stacks CPI, the 10y auction, TSMC sales and SoftBank.

red_flags.issue: Single-factor concentration has materialised: SOX/SMH/SOXX ~-12% on Nov 5 (worst since 2020), SOXX ~40% and SMH ~33% below highs; XLK -8% on the week. Expect high volatility into Nvidia (Nov 17).
